history_response.rule: Request, response, manifest and inner source-record limits are distinct. Manifest source record <=256 KiB; chunk source record <=2 MiB; every complete non-streaming send/relay/record/list-item/small-receipt JSON body <=8 MiB. All size admission uses final canonical bytes. Before durable high-water ack, complete response records/attestations are charged to max_unacked_response_bytes. Ack is valid only after durable disposition/install, atomically GC's the large record/attestation and releases active quota, while the compact exact HistoryKeyResponseSendReceipt ledger remains through request expiry for source retry. The compact ledger has independent request/requester/service hard limits and cannot admit a receipt if it would exceed them. Expiry converts it to a 30-day minimal tombstone. A limit failure occurs before enqueue. Staged blobs become sendable only with an atomic ready marker.
history_response.attempt_rule: Attempt identity is exactly (request_id,source_sender_domain,manifest response_id,manifest_digest). It is completed only after every descriptor-named chunk has a durable HistoryKeyResponseSendReceipt. v1 has no abandon operation: an unfinished attempt becomes expired only at request expiry; a permanent chunk rejection requires a new manifest but does not silently complete the old attempt. completed/expired atomically GC staged blobs and outbox bytes while compact accepted receipts remain through their normal ledger horizon. Only unfinished attempts count against the 4-per-source and 8-per-request concurrent limits. A request may create any number of sequential bounded manifests before expiry; there is no lifetime split/attempt cap.

governance_proof.rule: The stateless governance operation is only the near-current group_security_frontier selector. Its response is complete, independently verifiable, cursor-free and at most max_exact_response_bytes. Bulk or old history is reconstructed through receipt-bound direct accepted-Seal traversal and standard object/dependency resolve.

history_governance_traversal.rule: Member request ranges total at most 65,536 epochs; each RRK ArchiveListItem traversal has one singleton archive epoch. Before accepting a member request receipt or an organization-recovery archive replica, the service atomically pins the complete target-to-base accepted Seal cut, base Seal bodies, delta Control Moves, AvailabilityReceipts, signer-resolution evidence, external semantic dependencies and exact governance registry plus transitive replay-schema closure for the retention horizon. A member request replica does not promise or authorize governance traversal retention. Event/Seal resolve and governance-dependency resolve are caller-split point reads; dependency resolve is cursor-free and returns zero partial items on bounds failure. Disk-backed work queues and CAS dedupe bound memory without introducing a page/package/result-set wire.

archive_projection.rule: The fixed HPKE suite seals one closed single-secret plaintext. enc<=2048 base64url characters, ciphertext<=16384 characters and the complete public archive object<=32768 canonical bytes. Recipient-bound archive rows are canonical-byte paged and independently verifiable. A byte_limit below min_page_byte_limit is limit_exceeded; every admitted page limit can hold at least one maximum legal item plus framing, so limited pages cannot make zero progress.

quota_keys.origin_attribution_key: (material_key,origin_domain,origin_ref); origin_quota_domain is a separately persisted stable quota projection

history_store.material_dedupe_rule: Received secret bytes are globally deduplicated by material_key; origin never participates in material identity. A material instance receives one immutable monotonic material_received_sequence when bytes first become resident. The same bytes from a new origin add only CandidateOriginAttribution and never refresh that sequence. After bytes are evicted, a later refetch creates a new resident material instance and receives a new sequence.
history_store.origin_domain: Closed enum response_sender|rrk_archive|portable_backup. Stable origin_quota_domain is respectively {source_sender_domain}, {controller_id,holder_id,recovery_key_id,accepted_key_evidence_ref}, or {backup_series_id,producer_actor_id}. For RRK the accepted evidence EventId is the rotation identity; no independent key-version field exists. origin_ref is retrieval-only: {response_id,source_record_digest}, {container_event_ref,archive_digest}, or {backup_origin_id}; backup_origin_id is backup:<BackupId> or backup:sha256:<hex exact envelope bytes> and never a sender identity.
history_store.origin_attribution_rule: CandidateOriginAttribution key is exactly (material_key,origin_domain,origin_ref), while quotas use the separately persisted stable origin_quota_domain. The ledger admits at most 4 rows per material_key, 64 rows per exact (scope,group,epoch,origin_domain,origin_quota_domain), and 256 rows total per (scope,group,epoch). first_observed_at is immutable; expiry is computed as first_observed_at+2592000 seconds, is not stored, cannot be extended by duplicate/refetch, and timestamp overflow fails closed. Exact duplicate is a no-op. Before admission prune expired rows, then when any cap remains exceeded retain the minimum canonical tuple (first_observed_at,material_key.candidate_digest,origin_domain,JCS(origin_quota_domain),JCS(origin_ref)) and reject/prune larger rows. Origin attribution never duplicates bytes or changes material_received_sequence.
history_store.material_quota_rule: The 8-slot limit counts only resident received candidate material instances under material_key. local_authoritative material is stored in a separate accounting class, consumes no received slot, and is never evicted. CandidateOriginAttribution and EventCandidateBinding metadata consume no material slot and never pin bytes.
history_store.material_eviction_rule: Before inserting resident received material over quota, deterministically evict secret bytes in two tiers: first material with no success EventCandidateBinding, including unbound and failure-only; then success-bound material. Within a tier choose (material_received_sequence ascending,candidate_digest UTF-8 ascending). Success/failure bindings only select the tier and never pin bytes. Eviction deletes bytes plus the resident sequence only, preserves bounded origin attribution/Event binding tombstones for refetch, and never selects local_authoritative.
history_store.event_candidate_binding_rule: EventCandidateBinding key is exactly (event_binding_key,candidate_digest,outcome), where event_binding_key=(effective_scope,mls_group_id,epoch,event_id,verified_sender_domain) and outcome is success|failure. The suite-bearing event_id losslessly supplies the Event digest. The binding contains no origin and origin cannot be inferred from it. The independent ledger is capped at 256 rows per (scope,group,epoch); expiry is computed as immutable first_observed_at plus 2592000 seconds, is not stored, and timestamp overflow fails closed. Prune expired rows first, then (first_observed_at,event_id,verified_sender_domain,candidate_digest,outcome) canonical ascending. Pruning never changes the ciphertext replay ledger, material authority, or local_authoritative.
history_store.rule: Every received history secret remains a candidate; neither AEAD success nor failure promotes an epoch-wide winner. Candidate bytes and bounded Event attribution metadata are separate stores. A malicious sender's fake secret/ciphertext can affect only its signed Event attribution and cannot pin received material or exhaust all slots permanently. Portable backup writes only local_authoritative secrets.

backup.rule: Each object belongs to one exporter effective scope and is split by final encrypted bytes, never by guessed epoch count.

ordinary_download.rule: These limits apply only outside a verified RecoverySession. A deployment may choose a principal limit in the closed [16,64] range and may tighten the IP limits, but it cannot exceed the default 64-object principal ceiling.

recovery_session_unlock.rule: At the atomic transition to verified, the Station freezes the complete set of then-active, recoverable backup_id values and each exact object's canonical response-byte charge. The resulting server-side manifest is immutable and grants one independently consumed unlock allowance per entry plus a checked-u64 total byte budget equal to the sum of those charges. Manifest entries do not consume the ordinary 24-hour principal counter. Objects absent from the manifest, entries added or activated later, and a second use of a consumed allowance cannot borrow recovery quota. The Station MUST NOT enter verified when the remaining lifetime is no greater than completion_reserve_seconds or when its advertised byte/concurrency capacity cannot serve the manifest before the reserved deadline. It MUST admit at least the rate_formula rate, keyed by recovery_session_id rather than IP, while retaining fresh device proof, per-object unlock proof, byte-budget, concurrency, audit and one-use checks.

unlock_operation.rule: v1 defines no collection-level or batch unlock operation. Every request carries one complete object-bound proof and produces one object outcome; batching, partial outcomes and cross-object proof reuse require a future AKP.

requested_epoch_budget_rule: For canonical sorted, disjoint and non-adjacent requested_ranges, compute sum(to_epoch-from_epoch+1) with checked unsigned 64-bit arithmetic. Reject overflow or a sum above max_total_requested_epochs. Gaps between ranges are excluded.
global_identity_rule: HistoryRequestId and HistoryResponseId are globally unique object identities. Reuse of a response_id under another request response stream, requester, service or scope is duplicate_conflict; request_id plus sequence is only an internal pagination index and never a second identity namespace.
deployment_rule: A deployment may reject a new request earlier only if the smaller advertised limit is checked before acceptance. It cannot lower retention/size guarantees for already accepted objects or silently discard them.
